pamphlet_excerpts: Differences Between Continuous Tone Line: The half tone dots are so small, the human eye cannot see the individual dots unless they are magnified, but the eye does see an overall effect (p. 44).
Differences Between Continuous Tone Line Principle 2: The arrangement of the half tone dots creates this effect (p. 44).
Differences Between Continuous Tone Line Principle 3: The half tone dots in the part of an image that is supposed to look dark are big and fill most of the half tone dot area (p. 44).
Differences Between Continuous Tone Line Principle 4: The half tone dots in the part of an image that is supposed to look light are small and fill very little of thehalftone dot area (p. 44).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 (Differences Between Continuous Tone Line): Generally, half tones are made from a continuous-tone image, such as a traditional photograph (p. 44).
Step 2 (Differences Between Continuous Tone Line): In the past, the continuous-tone image was photographed through a special screen that created a half tone version of the original (p. 44).
Step 3 (Differences Between Continuous Tone Line): Today it is more common to take a continuous-tone image and scan it into a computer or to take a picture with a digital camera (p. 44).
Step 4 (Differences Between Continuous Tone Line): The computer software then converts the digital file into a pattern of small half tone dots that make up an image (p. 44).
